content.text:
{"prompt": "A square, full-bleed abstract painting in oil and cold wax on heavy canvas, with no frame, border, wall, room or gallery setting. It is entirely nonrepresentational: no objects, figures, faces, bodies, scenes, landscapes, horizons, machines, diagrams, symbols, icons, letters, numbers or text.

The composition has two opposed pressures. The left two-thirds is dense and turbulent, with hundreds of short, fast, overlapping palette-knife and dry-brush strokes in many directions. They are layered translucently, so earlier marks show through later ones as ghosts. This mass is packed with cold ultramarine, blackened teal, bruised violet and slate grey. Sharp slivers of hot vermilion and acid yellow-green break through it like small, urgent alarms. Near the center a few strokes of raw cadmium orange are scraped almost down to bare canvas, which gives the whole mass a feeling of strain.

The right third stays open. It is a wide, quiet field of pale bone white and faintly warm grey, thinly scumbled. Faint, slow, horizontal drags of a single dusty rose-gold smear across it, and the canvas weave shows through. A few isolated, deliberate strokes of deep indigo sit in this emptiness with plenty of space around them. They feel calm and unresolved, like a held breath.

Between the two zones, a long diagonal tear of thick impasto runs in jet black and titanium white, with a ridged, sculptural edge. Thin veils of glaze drip and bleed from it into both zones, so the turbulence and the stillness stay in tension without resolving. The rhythm is syncopated: clusters of tight, staccato marks, then long sweeping gestures, then silence. The texture ranges from glassy, smooth glazes to gritty, crusted paint, with visible bristle tracks, scraped-back layers, pentimenti and fingerprints of process. Lighting is flat and even so the paint surface does the work. The mood is intense, searching, honest and exposed, with some tenderness at the edges."}
